items.t: 69 houses sold in Kitsilano, Vancouver at a median of $2,680,000 (middle half $2,228,000 to $3,300,000). A typical house in Kitsilano, Vancouver spent 18 days on the market and closed at 96.7% of the asking price.

In Kitsilano, Vancouver, townhomes sold at a median of $1,405,000 across 70 sales, and the middle half closed between $1,178,250 and $1,757,500. The median townhome sat 12 days and sold for 98.2% of list.
Kitsilano, Vancouver: 240 condos sold at a median of $782,500, with the middle half between $649,975 and $949,925. The median condo took 14 days to sell and closed at 98.0% of list.

46 duplexes sold in Kitsilano, Vancouver at a median of $2,057,500 (middle half $1,833,000 to $2,567,500). A typical duplex in Kitsilano, Vancouver spent 15 days on the market and closed at 98.5% of the asking price.

How Kitsilano compares with the rest of Vancouver West

items.t: Houses in Kitsilano have the 13th highest median of 17 Vancouver West sub-areas, $2,680,000. University is lowest at $1,549,000 and Shaughnessy highest at $4,817,500. Mount Pleasant VW ($2,625,000) sits just below and S.W. Marine ($2,750,000) sits just above.

Of 18 Vancouver West sub-areas with 5 or more townhome sales, Kitsilano ranks 11th highest at $1,405,000; the range is $850,000 (False Creek) to $2,255,000 (Coal Harbour). University ($1,365,000) sits just below and South Granville ($1,450,000) sits just above.

Condos in Kitsilano have the 14th highest median of 21 Vancouver West sub-areas, $782,500. Marpole is lowest at $613,500 and Coal Harbour highest at $1,228,000. Southlands ($780,000) sits just below and South Cambie ($815,000) sits just above.

Of 9 Vancouver West sub-areas with 5 or more duplex sales, Kitsilano ranks 5th highest at $2,057,500; the range is $1,435,000 (Marpole) to $2,398,500 (Cambie). Point Grey ($2,055,750) sits just below and Arbutus ($2,075,000) sits just above.

blocks.text: By build year, duplexes are the newest homes selling in Kitsilano, Vancouver (median 2008) and houses the oldest (median 1929), a gap of 79 years.
